segments.text: Byron was at his best and most characteristic in the long poem
Childe Harold's Pilgrimage was a sensation that made his name
and Don Juan was a book-length virtuoso extravaganza that sealed the deal
but anyone who doubts that Byron could have shone if confined to shorter poems
should take a close look at this one and check out the perfection of his balance
one shade the more, one ray the less
it's just a tiny example of the impotence he could keep up for pages
the only thing that makes this particular Byronic poem non-Byronic
is that it professedly to do with innocence
the innocence is at the heart of the narrator's fancied young lady
and certainly she is more innocent than Byron truly thought life or love could ever be
but at the moment she is just a stack of iced cake
trembling in the slipstream as Byron sweeps by on his way to depravities
